title: Evidence Orchestrator: control-mapping and automated collectors for SOC2/ISO27001
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and deliver an Evidence Orchestrator feature that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 control frameworks, orchestrates automated collectors (config snapshots, KV cache retention logs, routing decisions, KMS access logs, network policy manifests), and produces attestation-ready artifacts and reports for auditors. The goal is to reduce manual evidence collection time for customers and internal compliance by >80% for common controls, and enable per-region data residency proof and configurable retention proofs.

Scope: 
- Control mapping registry: canonical mapping file that links Redwood product controls to SOC2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A controls, with notes on evidence types and acceptable artifacts.
- Collector framework: lightweight agents/queries run in hosted and private deployments to capture periodic snapshots and streaming evidence. Collectors include: config-export, model-serving-metrics, KV-cache-eviction-log, request-routing-audit, kms-access-events, s3-lifecycle-policy-snapshot, and console-access-audit.
- Evidence packaging: signed artifacts (zip + manifest) with hash chain and KMS-backed signing metadata for auditor consumption.
- Reporting/console UX: a Compliance Evidence page showing mapped controls, last-collected timestamp, retention provenance, and per-region residency assertions.
- Automation rules: scheduling, frequency presets (daily/weekly/monthly), and retention-proof templates (e.g., retention policy + deletion confirmation).

Out of scope for initial tranche: full automated remediation and third-party attestation filing.

Success metrics:
- Time to produce evidence bundle for SOC2-common-controls reduced from median 16 hours manual to under 2 hours automated.
- >70% of SOC2 in-scope controls covered by automated collectors in v1.

Non-functional requirements:
- Evidence collectors must support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) deployment modes.
- Proof artifacts must be immutable and auditable for configurable retention windows.
- Respect data residency: artifacts containing customer data must include region metadata and follow customer retention settings.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMPLIANCE/pages/Evidence+Orchestrator+Spec
- Prototype UI mock (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Compliance-Evidence-UI

- Engineering spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/489
- Related PM ticket: PM-4602 (Retention settings policy UX)
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping registry exists and covers at least 70% of SOC2 common controls with evidence type annotations

At least five automated collectors implemented and runnable in hosted and private environments (config-export, kms-access-events, request-routing-audit, kv-cache-eviction-log, s3-lifecycle-policy-snapshot)
Console shows per-control last-collected timestamp and region-residency assertion
Evidence bundle generation produces signed artifact with manifest, hash, and collection log
Automated runbook documents for auditors (Confluence) and internal ops are published

design_notes: Evidence page should present controls grouped by framework (SOC2 / ISO27001) with toggle to view only controls mapped to a customer's subscription tier
Artifact downloads must show signed timestamp and region metadata; provide machine-readable manifest.json alongside human-readable summary
Retention settings UI in PM-4602 will feed into collector scheduling and artifact pruning; show effective retention in evidence bundle
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike & map): finalize control mapping and implement 3 core collectors in hosted staging (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Collector hardening): support private deployments and add KMS signing integration; implement retention hooks (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Console + packaging): UI, artifact signing, and export flows; prepare runbooks and auditor docs (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (Pilot & feedback): onboard 3 customers for pilot and collect feedback for gap remediation (2 weeks)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Collectors may capture PII or sensitive tokens accidentally. Mitigation: collectors must apply redaction rules and respect data residency filters; require security sign-off before pilot.
Risk: Private deployment constraints (air-gapped) prevent automated upload. Mitigation: provide offline collector mode that produces signed bundles which customers can upload manually.
Risk: Auditor requirements vary by firm. Mitigation: keep mapping extensible and allow customers to attach custom artifacts to control evidence entries.
